title: Rafal and the Robotic Pinky
subtitle: One small fracture. One huge upgrade. One very sore loser.
description: Mom handles the hospital trip. Dad diagnoses a top-secret gaming upgrade. Then Rafal starts beating him at everything. Coincidence? Dad would like a rematch.
cover_alt: Rafal in black rectangular glasses and a dark cyan-trimmed hoodie holds up his right palm. The silver device is on his smallest, outermost finger. Kyan stands beside him in an orange hoodie, without glasses.
note: A fictional adventure inspired by a real family moment. The splint is for healing; the AI is part of the joke. Follow the treating clinician’s advice about recovery and returning to games and sport.

pages.title: The update nobody ordered
paragraphs: Rafal could dodge a wall of spikes in Geometry Dash. A ball in P.E., apparently, was a different difficulty setting.
It hit his right pinky head-on. His smallest finger immediately submitted the largest possible complaint.
Kyan hurried over. “You okay?”
“My finger just rage-quit.”
The teacher called Mom. She rushed Rafal to the hospital, where he discovered that real life had neither a pause button nor an option to reload his last save.
“Can we skip the hospital level?” he asked.
Mom gave him a look. “No shortcuts on this one.”
For once, Rafal did not argue with the administrator.
pages.caption: P.E. has terrible respawn mechanics.
pages.alt: Rafal, wearing rectangular glasses, and Kyan on the school court at the moment a ball hits Rafal’s bare right little finger.

pages.title: Hardware installation
paragraphs: The X-ray showed a small fracture. The doctor fitted a metal splint to keep Rafal’s right pinky straight while it healed.
A couple of weeks in the splint. Follow the instructions. Let the finger recover. Mom listened carefully; Rafal stared at the shiny new hardware.
“Does it come in black?” he asked.
“It comes in ‘please look after it,’” said Mom.
When they got home, Dad took one look and went completely silent.
This was unusual. Usually, getting Dad to stop talking required a software update.
Then he leaned closer.
“They gave you a robotic finger.”
Rafal sighed. The fracture was small. The story Dad was about to tell was not.
pages.caption: One small splint. An unlimited supply of dad jokes.
pages.alt: Mom supports Rafal at the hospital while he examines the metal splint on the smallest outer finger of his right hand. Rafal wears rectangular glasses.

pages.title: Meet PINK-E 9000
paragraphs: “Not just any robotic finger,” Dad announced when Kyan came over. “PINK-E 9000. Advanced AI. Predictive gaming. Tactical brilliance.”
“It’s a splint,” said Rafal.
“That’s what they want you to think.”
Kyan examined it without touching it. “Where’s the charging port?”
“Wireless.”
“Where’s the battery?”
“Classified.”
“Where’s the evidence?”
Dad pointed at himself. “I work in technology.”
Rafal adjusted his glasses. “That is not how evidence works.”
“Fine. We’ll settle this in Minecraft.”
Once Mom was satisfied that a short session fitted the doctor’s instructions, the test began. Rafal kept the splinted pinky protected. The alleged AI would have to do its work wirelessly.
pages.caption: Source: Dad. Confidence level: Dad.
pages.alt: Rafal raises his right palm beside Kyan in an imagined neon gaming city; only the smallest finger, opposite the thumb, has the silver device.

pages.title: Bed Wars. Dad loses.
paragraphs: Dad built a fortress around his bed. Extra blocks. Extra layers. The sort of defence that said, ‘I watched half a tutorial.’
“Try getting through that,” he said.
Rafal went around it.
Kyan watched Dad’s bed disappear. Then Dad disappeared. Then, for several beautiful seconds, Dad’s commentary disappeared.
“The robotic finger,” Dad said at last. “It predicted my entire strategy.”
“Your entire strategy was ‘more blocks,’” said Kyan.
“Exactly. An extremely complex algorithm.”
Rafal won the rematch too.
Dad checked his mouse. His keyboard. His connection.
“Interesting,” said Rafal. “The AI seems to be working on all your excuses.”
pages.caption: Defence budget: enormous. Actual defence: questionable.
pages.alt: Rafal and Kyan celebrate in front of a block-built Bed Wars arena; Rafal’s right little finger is protected by its silver splint.

pages.title: The commentary bug
paragraphs: Next came Geometry Dash. Rafal settled into the rhythm. Kyan watched the progress counter climb.
“Observe,” Dad whispered, very loudly. “The AI is calculating the perfect—”
The cube hit a spike.
Rafal turned slowly.
“—learning opportunity,” Dad finished.
Kyan opened an imaginary support ticket. “Bug found: background process called Dad.exe.”
“Can we close it?” asked Rafal.
Dad pretended to freeze.
On the next attempt, Rafal sailed through the section that had been giving him trouble. Kyan cheered. Dad remained impressively quiet.
“Best update so far,” said Rafal.
Dad unfroze just long enough to say, “You’re welcome.”
pages.caption: Recommended setting: commentary off.
pages.alt: Rafal, in glasses and a dark cyan-trimmed hoodie, concentrates in front of glowing geometric obstacles. His right little finger is protected by the silver splint.

pages.title: Four lines. Zero excuses.
paragraphs: Tetris was supposed to be Dad’s comeback.
“I was playing this before you were born,” he said.
“So your training data is old,” Rafal replied.
Dad’s stack climbed. Rafal left a narrow gap, waited, and dropped the long piece. Four lines vanished.
Dad stared.
Rafal did it again.
“That finger is predicting the future.”
Kyan pointed at the screen. “There’s literally a next-piece preview.”
“It’s predicting the preview.”
Rafal won. Dad requested a rematch. Rafal won that too.
“I demand a hardware inspection,” Dad announced.
“Mom already did one,” said Rafal. “At the hospital.”
Kyan nearly fell off his chair.
pages.caption: Dad’s experience: decades. Dad’s wins: currently unavailable.
pages.alt: Close-up of a glowing falling-block puzzle, with brightly coloured tetrominoes and a narrow vertical gap.

pages.title: Peer-reviewed by Kyan
paragraphs: Kyan opened a notebook. “Let’s review the evidence.”
Rafal had beaten Dad in Minecraft Bed Wars. Rafal had beaten Dad in Tetris. Dad had developed fourteen new explanations for losing.
“Conclusion,” Kyan said. “The finger is either advanced AI, or Rafal is just better than you.”
Dad considered both possibilities for less than a second.
“Definitely advanced AI.”
“Can it do my homework?” Rafal asked.
“No. That feature requires the premium plan.”
“What’s the price?”
“Doing your homework.”
Mom appeared in the doorway. “The free plan includes taking a break.”
Every screen went quiet. Apparently, even PINK-E 9000 respected parental controls.
pages.caption: An independent study. Except for all the participants.
pages.alt: Kyan, without glasses, grins in his orange hoodie and headphones, delighted by the gaming results.

pages.title: It must be real
paragraphs: A few weeks later, Mom took Rafal back for his check-up. The doctor said the splint could come off.
Dad looked delighted. “Excellent. A fair match at last.”
Once Rafal was cleared to play normally again, they tried Tetris.
Rafal won.
Then Minecraft Bed Wars.
Rafal won again.
Dad stared at the retired splint on the desk. “The AI must have transferred into your brain.”
Kyan folded his arms. “So the AI wasn’t real?”
“Of course it was,” said Dad. “It’s on the website.”
Rafal opened It Must Be Real. There they were: the finger, the story, and an extremely detailed record of Dad losing.
“See?” Rafal said. “Verified.”
Dad leaned towards the screen.
“Can we at least edit the score?”
pages.caption: One finger healed. One gaming reputation still in recovery.
pages.alt: At his follow-up, Rafal smiles in his rectangular glasses and raises his bare right hand. The splint is no longer worn.
